regulations.area: Humboldt Bay to Cape Mendocino · California · Northern Groundfish Management Area
regulations.scope: Reviewed 2026 official recreational boat rules within the Crescent City–Del Norte, Humboldt Bay–Cape Mendocino and Trinidad–Klamath browse footprints. Ocean day trips only, not inland river fishing. In-season closures, exact MPA geometry, method, harbor and route clearance remain separate checks.
common_notes: Northern Management Area is Oregon border to 40°10′ N. MPA and federal closures are position- and method-specific. A boat depth limit is not a legal depth boundary.
A regional rules card is not an open-season or exact-position clearance. Fresh source status, MPA geometry, method and in-season access remain separate checks.
When taking finfish from a boat, have a landing net with an opening at least 18 inches in diameter available for immediate use to land undersized fish. Do not gaff an undersized fish (§28.65).

rules-gear.name: CDFW finfish gear and general rules
rules-gear.review_note: Read section 28.65 and the July 3 effective emergency language. Groundfish aboard restricts to one line/two hooks; salmon has separate rod/barbless rules. Landing net opening at least 18 inches is required for boat finfish, and undersized fish cannot be gaffed. New wire/large-hook shore restrictions are south of Pigeon Point, not this Northern footprint. Added the omitted landing-net reminder; no Northern hook permission was expanded.

rules-invertebrates.name: CDFW invertebrate gear rules
rules-invertebrates.review_note: Read sections 29.80 and 29.85 with the January 1, 2026 approved crab gear language. Preserve private-boat ten-trap/validation, nine-day tending, seven-day pre-opener prohibition, six-loop snare and two-hour hoop inspection rules. Northern hoop buoy is at most 6 by 14 inches; optional orange H marker and surface-line markings differ from trap buoys. Season, toxin closures and trap declarations remain separate gates.

rules-whales.name: CDFW whale-safe crab restrictions
rules-whales.review_note: Read the 2026-27 status and dated prior-season assessments: recreational and commercial seasons currently closed. June 2026 commercial Zones 1-2 depth/gear reductions and recreational Zones 3-5 trap prohibitions do not clear Northern recreational traps for November. No new-season recreational clearance is established. Approve the closed/scheduled representation only; preserve requires_opening_review and trap requires_clearance, rather than infer clearance from zone latitude or an old declaration.

rules-health.name: CDFW fishery health closures
rules-health.review_note: Read current health status: Del Norte razor clams closed October 9, Humboldt razor clams remain closed; Monterey anchovy consumption restrictions are outside these footprints. No current recreational Dungeness toxin closure is listed, but this is not a season opening, trap clearance or November health forecast. Commercial rock-crab closures are not private-boat Dungeness rules. Keep trip-time health checks and scheduled crab opener.

rules-ocean.name: CDFW official regulation index
rules-ocean.review_note: Read CDFW ocean index as the authoritative source directory and followed Northern rules, booklet, in-season and Commission links. An index is not evidence of an open season or exact-position access. Species conclusions use the detailed legal records; no catch, habitat or navigation claim is derived from this page.

rules-groundfish.name: CDFW groundfish
rules-groundfish.review_note: Read Northern groundfish summary and linked table alongside approved regular language effective May 19. Northern boat season is April 1-December 31 at all depths, not the Mendocino split-depth schedule. Retain descending-device, one-line/two-hook, RCG ten, one copper/two canary/four vermilion-sunset and prohibited-species restrictions; lingcod two at 22 inches remains separate.

rules-inseason.name: CDFW in-season changes
rules-inseason.review_note: Read dated changes through October 9. July 28 notice closes KMZ recreational salmon; August San Francisco modifications do not reopen Northern waters. October Del Norte razor-clam closure does not change the seven displayed species. Commercial Northern crab depth restrictions and Central recreational trap restrictions are not a new Northern recreational opener. No listed Pacific-halibut quota closure overrides the retained conditional season as of retrieval.

rules-salmon.name: CDFW salmon
rules-salmon.review_note: Read current salmon guidance with section 27.80 and in-season flyer. KMZ (Oregon border to 40 degrees 10 minutes N) remains closed for the rest of 2026; no fall opener transfers north. Salmon vessel possession is prohibited in closed KMZ. Section 27.75 Klamath mouth closure is year-round for salmon and expands in August; these limits do not certify other-species access or inland fishing. Keep empty salmon windows.

rules-crab.name: CDFW crab
rules-crab.review_note: Read recreational regulations and 2026 FAQ, distinguishing commercial notices and CPFV passenger validation exceptions from this private-boat profile. Northern hoop changes are effective January 1, 2026, not pending. A trap restriction does not itself prohibit hoop/snare take, but neither method may bypass season/health closures. Ten Dungeness at 5.75 inches applies only when open; November 7 remains scheduled, not cleared.

rules-book.name: CDFW 2026 ocean sport fishing booklet
rules-book.review_note: Read July 17 updated booklet sections 27.25, 27.65, 27.75, 27.80, 28.15, 28.20, 28.27, 28.38, 28.55, 28.65, 29.80, 29.85 and Northern section 632 entries. Corrected a substantive error: section 27.65's California-halibut fillet exception is SOUTH of Point Arena; Northern boat filleting/steaking/chunking and landing such pieces are prohibited. Pacific/California halibut remain distinct. Later KMZ in-season closure supersedes booklet summer openings. Reading Rock method exceptions do not remove whole-MPA exclusion.

rules-proposals.name: California FGC rulemaking: effective and pending changes
rules-proposals.review_note: Read 2026 index and continuing 2025 entries plus linked approved text. Effective: Pacific halibut March 12; salmon May 16 with later in-season closure; regular groundfish May 19; white-shark emergency July 3-December 31; crab gear January 1. October 14 adoption of white-shark extension still has pending OAL/effective fields; sport-fishing and tuna-harpoon proposals likewise are not operative permission. Do not use expired groundfish emergency extension as current authority. Inland Klamath section 7.40 is outside this ocean-only scope.

rules-tuna-federal.name: Federal recreational Pacific tuna rules · 50 CFR 660.721
rules-tuna-federal.review_note: Read exact eCFR section 660.721 despite unchanged fingerprint. Northern albacore limit is 25; entering U.S. EEZ south of 34 degrees 27 minutes N limits the whole trip to ten. Per-24-hour-at-sea and one-calendar-day bag constraints remain. State section 28.38 adds albacore to general finfish limit; this review is day trips, not multi-day possession or Mexican waters.

rules-salmon-pdf.name: CDFW 2026 ocean salmon season flyer · August update
rules-salmon-pdf.review_note: Read complete official flyer, August 19 update with October 6 version footer. KMZ 3,900 Chinook guideline attained and August dates closed; fall only south of 38 degrees 02 minutes N. Smith/Klamath mouth salmon closures and August Klamath Control Zone persist. Closed KMZ vessel possession is not a transit exception. Seasonal closure is retained; no 2027 permission is asserted.

rules-groundfish-pdf.name: CDFW Northern groundfish season table
rules-groundfish-pdf.review_note: Read the unchanged Northern table rather than assume unchanged means accepted. April-December all-depth boat season, RCG ten including one copper/two canary/four vermilion-sunset, no yelloweye/quillback/cowcod/bronzespotted, lingcod two at 22 inches and descending-device duty match final profiles and May 19 regular law. This is not a legal-location or bottom-depth clearance.

rules-northern.name: CDFW Northern Region rules
rules-northern.review_note: Read October 9 Northern summary covering all three footprints north of 40 degrees 10 minutes N. California halibut two/22 inches year-round; Pacific halibut one/no minimum through November 15 or quota; KMZ salmon closed; Dungeness season closed with November 7 scheduled only. Northern table controls groundfish. New razor-clam/sturgeon text does not add species to this registry. Correct California-halibut processing by booklet, not an inferred Southern exception.

mpa-pyramid.name: CDFW Pyramid Point SMCA
mpa-pyramid.review_note: Read current Pyramid Point page and booklet section 632(b)(1). Recreational true-smelt dip/Hawaiian-net exception and named tribal exemption do not allow ordinary reef/halibut fishing. Preserve Crescent City dependency and conservative exclusion of the whole mapped MPA; Trinidad promotion removes no neighboring protection.

mpa-st-george.name: CDFW Point St. George Reef Offshore SMCA
mpa-st-george.review_note: Read current Point St. George Reef Offshore page and booklet section 632(b)(2). Recreational salmon trolling and Dungeness by trap are narrow exceptions, subject to seasons/trap restrictions; commercial and tribal provisions are not general permission. Retain whole-MPA exclusion and existing Crescent City sources.

mpa-reading.name: CDFW Reading Rock MPAs
mpa-reading.review_note: Read Reading Rock page, both linked facts/regulation PDFs and current booklet sections 632(b)(6)-(7). SMR prohibits marine-resource take; SMCA permits recreational salmon trolling, true smelt (page says surf smelt) by dip/Hawaiian throw net and Dungeness by trap/hoop/hand, plus named tribal exemptions. No general rockfish/lingcod/halibut exception. Updated notice distinguishes methods while retaining conservative exclusion of BOTH whole MPAs. Direct Westlaw fetch was unavailable and is not claimed inspected.

rules-pacific-halibut.name: CDFW Pacific halibut season and quota
rules-pacific-halibut.review_note: Read current Pacific-halibut page, Northern status and March 12 effective section 28.20. North of Point Arena: April 1-November 15 OR earlier quota closure, one fish/no minimum, one line/two hooks when angling. No current closure notice was present; catch tracking is not a prediction or clearance. Preserve quota warning and source dependencies so later notices withhold open; south-of-Point-Arena December dates do not transfer north.

mpa-samoa.name: CDFW Samoa SMCA
mpa-samoa.review_note: Read current Samoa SMCA page and booklet section 632(b)(8): recreational salmon trolling, true-smelt nets and Dungeness trap/hoop/hand exceptions, with separate Wiyot exemption. They do not open reef/halibut fishing or supersede seasons. Preserve Humboldt notice dependency and whole-MPA target exclusion; this existing footprint is not silently dropped.

mpa-south-humboldt.name: CDFW South Humboldt Bay SMRMA
mpa-south-humboldt.review_note: Read South Humboldt Bay SMRMA page and booklet section 632(b)(9). Marine resource take prohibition, waterfowl under separate hunting regulations and named Wiyot exemption are not ordinary fishing permission. Preserve existing Humboldt protected-area notice and complete mapped exclusion.

mpa-south-cape.name: CDFW South Cape Mendocino SMR and special closures
mpa-south-cape.review_note: Read South Cape Mendocino/Sugarloaf/Steamboat page and booklet section 632 entries. Reserve prohibits marine-resource take; Sugarloaf has year-round 300-foot vessel restriction and Steamboat March-August 300-foot restriction, with specified official/emergency exceptions. Preserve Humboldt footprint, local notice dependencies and conservative protected-geometry exclusion; no operational access is certified.

lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Northern Management Area.
lingcod.bag: 2 per person daily; 2 in possession. Separate from the 10-fish RCG limit.
details: Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting lingcod, or when lingcod are aboard. Your double-drop rig fits that limit.
Carry a descending device ready for immediate use.
Fillets aboard: at least 14 in, with all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

rockfish.name: Rockfish / rock cod
rockfish.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Northern Management Area.
rockfish.bag: 10 total rockfish, cabezon and greenlings combined per person daily and in possession.
rockfish.size: No minimum length for retained rockfish. Species must be identified.
details: Within the 10: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 4 vermilion/sunset rockfish combined.
No retention of yelloweye, quillback, cowcod or bronzespotted rockfish.
Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting rockfish, or when rockfish are aboard. Carry a descending device ready for use.
Retained rockfish fillets must have all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.season: California halibut: year-round in the reviewed 2026 Northern rules; distinct from Pacific halibut.
halibut.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession north of Point Sur.
details: California halibut only; Pacific halibut has a different season and rules.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply. With rockfish or lingcod aboard, use one line and no more than two hooks; salmon aboard triggers salmon gear rules.

Do not fillet, steak or cut California halibut into chunks aboard a boat or bring it ashore in those forms in this Northern footprint. The §27.65 California-halibut fillet exception applies only south of Point Arena, not here. Do not gaff an undersized fish.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.season: Ocean salmon is closed in the Klamath Management Zone for the remainder of 2026.
salmon.bag: No retention while the Northern/Klamath recreational season is closed.
salmon.size: Not applicable during the 2026 closed season.
details: CDFW says the Klamath Management Zone remains closed for the rest of 2026; do not use a Central/Southern fall opener here.
Future seasons depend on federal and state action and require a new review.

The Klamath River mouth has a year-round ocean salmon closure under §27.75(b), expanding into the Klamath Control Zone in August. These are salmon-specific closures, not a blanket authorization or prohibition for other species. Consult exact boundaries; inland river fishing is outside this review.
Salmon may not be possessed aboard a vessel in the Klamath Management Zone while its salmon season is closed (§27.80). A catch from another management area does not authorize transit possession here.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.season: Year-round in reviewed 2026 state and federal rules, subject to current notices in U.S. waters north of Point Conception.
albacore.bag: 25 per person daily and in possession, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
albacore.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The albacore limit drops to 10 south of Point Conception (34°27′ N). This card does not cover Mexico.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard south of Point Conception, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. This card covers day trips; multi-day possession rules differ.
If any part of an albacore trip enters U.S. EEZ waters south of 34°27′ N, no more than 10 albacore per person may be onboard for that trip; the rule is not determined only by where a fish was caught.
Federal tuna limits apply per 24-hour period at sea and never authorize more than one daily bag per calendar day. Multi-day possession needs separate review.

South of Point Conception (34°27′ N), tuna processed aboard must use the six-piece arrangement required by §27.65, keep all skin attached, and be individually bagged with its species labeled. That specific six-piece rule does not apply to processing north of the line.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.season: Closed after Jul 31, 2026. Nov 7, 2026 is a scheduled reopening, subject to health and gear declarations.
dungeness.bag: When open: 10 per person daily; 10 in possession on a private boat.
dungeness.size: 5¾ in shell width, measured across the body just in front of the side spines, excluding those spines. Carry a crab gauge.
details: Season opening and trap permission are separate. Northern November trap clearance has not been confirmed; check CDFW whale-safe and health notices.
A crab-trap validation is required to use traps. Maximum 10 deployed traps per person; required escape rings, destruct device, GO ID and buoy markings apply.
Hoop nets and snares have separate gear rules. A trap restriction does not itself close those methods, but the season and health closures still apply.
Check the current 2026 hoop-net marking rules and all gear details in §29.80 before setting gear.
Crab traps may not be deployed during the seven days before the Dungeness season opens. Service deployed traps at intervals no greater than nine days, weather conditions permitting (§29.80(c)).
Crab loop traps or snares may have no more than six loops. Hoop nets must be raised and inspected at least every two hours (§29.80).

North of Point Arguello, each hoop net must have the required surface buoy marked with the operator’s GO ID; the main buoy may not exceed 6 in in diameter or 14 in in length. An optional orange marker marked H and its connecting line have additional marking specifications; check §29.80(b) before rigging.

trap.note: Trap permission is checked separately from the Dungeness season and health closures. Confirm the current recreational trap declaration, validation, marking and tending rules before setting.

hoop.note: A hoop net is a different gear category from a crab trap. Follow the current hoop-net construction, attendance and deployment rules; season and health closures still apply.

snare.note: Use the current snare definition and gear limits. A trap restriction does not by itself establish permission to take Dungeness; the season and health checks also apply.

pacific-halibut.name: Pacific halibut
pacific-halibut.season: Apr 1–Nov 15, 2026 north of Point Arena, or until the quota is reached earlier.
details: When angling, use no more than one line with two hooks attached.
Quota can close the season early; check the current CDFW halibut page and hotline before fishing.
Pacific halibut is distinct from California halibut; do not apply the two-fish California halibut limit.
Check the exact MPA, method and all other gear rules at the selected position and date.

rod.note: This profile covers recreational boat angling. One line with a maximum of two hooks; quota and geographic notices still apply.

area_notices.name: Northern California MPAs
area_notices.note: Reading Rock SMR prohibits take of living, geological and cultural marine resources. Reading Rock SMCA permits recreational salmon by trolling, true smelt by dip net or Hawaiian throw net, and Dungeness crab by trap, hoop net or hand, subject to other seasons and restrictions; named tribal exemptions are separate. Pyramid Point and Point St. George Reef Offshore have different exceptions. The app conservatively excludes each whole mapped MPA from fishing targets, including the SMCA; this is not an exception-aware fishing permission. Consult exact coordinates and methods in §632.

area_notices.name: Klamath mouth and ocean salmon closures
area_notices.note: Ocean salmon is closed throughout the Klamath Management Zone for the remainder of 2026, with no vessel possession during closure. The Klamath River mouth has a year-round salmon closure that expands in August into the Klamath Control Zone (§27.75(b)); exact boundaries matter. These are salmon-specific restrictions, not blanket clearance for other species. Inland river rules, river-bar access and route safety are not covered by this ocean preview.

area_notices.name: Humboldt Bay and Cape Mendocino protected areas
area_notices.note: Samoa SMCA has narrow salmon, surf smelt and Dungeness take exceptions; South Humboldt Bay SMRMA and South Cape Mendocino SMR prohibit most take. Sugarloaf Island and Steamboat Rock have vessel-access restrictions. The app excludes mapped protected geometries from fishing targets; inspect exact CDFW boundaries and method/date exceptions.

limitations: Landing port is not a catch position; named grounds are broad reports, not GPS fixes.
Reports are a selected sample, with unknown effort and missing unsuccessful trips.
Satellite temperature and HF radar measure surface context, not bottom conditions.
Daily observations are not a seven-day bite forecast or live entrance clearance.
